nodes.summary: For graphons $U, W$ with values in $[0, 1]$ and every simple graph $F$, The proof is the telescoping argument of the finite counting lemma, with sums replaced by integrals.
nodes.title: Counting lemma for graphons

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a simple graph and let $w, w'$ be weighted graphs on the same finite vertex set with all edge weights in $[0, 1]$. Then So homomorphism densities are Lipschitz in the cut distance: graphs that are close in the cut norm have close subgraph densities. The proof changes one edge weight at a time; each step is the integral of $(w - w')(x_i, x_j)$ against factors in $[0,1]$ that depend on $x_i$ alone or on…
nodes.title: Counting lemma

nodes.summary: For `a, b : V → [0, 1]`, `|∑_{x, y} a(x) b(y) u(x, y)| ≤ max_{S, T} |∑_{x ∈ S, y ∈ T} u(x, y)|` (Borgs–Chayes–Lovász–Sós– Vesztergombi, *Convergent sequences of dense graphs I*, Adv. Math. 219 (2008), equation (3.3), finite form).
nodes.title: Bilinear forms are bounded by the cut norm

nodes.summary: The `0`/`1` weights of a simple graph lie in `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Simple-graph weights lie in the unit interval

nodes.summary: The `0`/`1` weighted graph of a simple graph `G`: weight `1` on the edges of `G` and `0` on non-edges and loops.
nodes.title: Edge weight of a simple graph

nodes.summary: Refining by two sets multiplies the number of classes by at most `4`.
nodes.title: Refinement multiplies the number of classes by at most four

nodes.summary: Integrating out the two endpoints of an edge `uv` bounds the contribution of a kernel `D` on that edge, multiplied by `[0, 1]`-valued factors on the other edges, by the cut norm of `D` (Lovász–Szegedy, proof of Lemma 4.1).
nodes.title: One telescoping step of the counting lemma

nodes.summary: Two graphons $U, W$ with values in $[0, 1]$ satisfy $\delta_\square(U, W) = 0$ if and only if $t(F, U) = t(F, W)$ for every simple graph $F$. So the graphon limit of a convergent graph sequence is unique up to cut distance $0$ (weak isomorphism).
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the limit

nodes.summary: For graphons $U$ and $W$, the infimum over pairs of measure-preserving maps $\varphi, \psi$ of $[0, 1]$. It is only a pseudometric: $\delta_\square(W, W^\varphi) = 0$, and the step functions of a graph and of its blow-ups are at distance $0$. The infimum can equivalently be taken over couplings of the uniform distribution with itself, or over measure-preserving bijections.
nodes.title: Cut distance of graphons

nodes.summary: The quantity `max_{S, T ⊆ V} |∑_{x ∈ S} ∑_{y ∈ T} u(x, y)|` of `u : Sym2 V → ℝ` (the matrix cut norm `‖A‖_□` of Lovász–Szegedy, §4.1).
nodes.title: Unnormalized cut norm

nodes.summary: The cut norm of every kernel is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the cut norm

nodes.summary: The cut norm of a symmetric kernel $u : \operatorname{Sym}^2 V \to \mathbb R$ on a finite vertex set is For two weighted graphs $w, w'$ on the same vertex set, $\|w - w'\|_\square$ is their cut (rectangle) distance $d_\square$: two independent random graphs $G(n, 1/2)$ are close in cut distance with high probability (the distance tends to $0$), although they differ in about half of their pairs.
nodes.title: Cut norm

nodes.summary: The admissible pairs `(S, T)` in the cut norm: measurable subsets of `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Measurable rectangles of the unit square

nodes.summary: For weights `a ∈ [0, 1]`, the weighted sum `∑ a x * g x` is bounded in absolute value by the sum of `g` over some subset (the set where `g` has the sign of the weighted sum).
nodes.title: Weighted sums are bounded by subset sums

nodes.summary: For every $\varepsilon > 0$, every weighted graph $G$ on a finite vertex set (unit node weights) has a partition $\mathcal P$ of its vertices into at most $4^{1/\varepsilon^2}$ classes such that where $G_{\mathcal P}$ is the partition average and $\|G\|_2 = (|V|^{-2} \sum_{x,y} \beta_{xy}^2)^{1/2}$. Compared with Szemerédi's regularity lemma, the number of classes is only exponential in $1/\varepsilon^2$ instead of…
nodes.title: Weak regularity lemma (Frieze–Kannan)

nodes.summary: For every graphon $W$ there is a sequence of nonempty simple graphs $G_n$ with $t(F, G_n) \to t(F, W)$ for every simple graph $F$. One can take the $W$-random graphs $G(n, W)$: pick $x_1, \dots, x_n$ uniformly in $[0, 1]$ and join $i$ and $j$ with probability $W(x_i, x_j)$; with probability $1$ this sequence converges to $W$.
nodes.title: Every graphon is a graph limit

nodes.summary: Every convergent sequence of nonempty simple graphs $G_n$ has a graphon limit: there is a graphon $W$ (symmetric, measurable, values in $[0, 1]$) such that Lovász and Szegedy prove more: the limits of $t(\cdot, G_n)$ are exactly the graph parameters of the form $t(\cdot, W)$, and also exactly the normalized, multiplicative, reflection-positive parameters.
nodes.title: Lovász–Szegedy limit theorem

nodes.summary: If the partition average $w_{\mathcal P}$ is not $\varepsilon$-close to $w$ in the cut norm, i.e. $\|w - w_{\mathcal P}\|_\square > \varepsilon \|w\|_2$, then some partition $\mathcal Q$ with at most four times as many classes as $\mathcal P$ (the refinement by the two sets of a witnessing rectangle) has energy larger than $E(\mathcal P) + \varepsilon^2 \sum_{x,y} w(x,y)^2$.
nodes.title: One refinement step

nodes.summary: Every sequence of graphons $W_n$ (values in $[0, 1]$) has a subsequence $W_{n_k}$ and a graphon $W$ with $\delta_\square(W_{n_k}, W) \to 0$. Equivalently, after identifying graphons at cut distance $0$, the space of graphons with the cut distance is a compact metric space; since simple graphs are dense in it, it is the completion of the space of graphs in the cut distance.
nodes.title: Compactness of the graphon space

nodes.summary: For a bounded measurable kernel $W$ on $[0,1]^2$, the supremum over measurable $S, T$. It is within a factor $4$ of the $L^\infty \to L^1$ operator norm of $W$, and at most $\|W\|_1$. In Lean the supremum is taken in $\mathbb R$; it is meaningful for bounded kernels, for which it is finite.
nodes.title: Cut norm of a kernel

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $F$ on $\{1, \dots, k\}$ and a graphon $W$, each edge counted once. If $W_G$ is the step function of a graph $G$ (constant $\beta_{ij}$ on the square of side $1/|V(G)|$ indexed by $i, j$), then $t(F, W_G) = t(F, G)$.
nodes.title: Homomorphism density in a graphon

nodes.summary: For simple graphs $F$ and $G$ on finite vertex sets, where $\hom(F, G)$ is the number of graph homomorphisms $F \to G$ (Mathlib's `F →g G`) and $t(F, G)$ is the homomorphism density of $F$ in the $0/1$ weighted graph of $G$.
nodes.title: Homomorphism density counts homomorphisms

nodes.summary: The density of an edgeless graph in any weighted graph with a vertex is `1` (homomorphism densities are *normalized*, Lovász–Szegedy, *Limits of dense graph sequences*, §2.2).
nodes.title: Homomorphism densities are normalized

nodes.summary: Densities in a weighted graph with edge weights in `[0, 1]` are at most `1`.
nodes.title: Homomorphism densities are at most one

nodes.summary: Densities in a weighted graph with nonnegative edge weights are nonnegative.
nodes.title: Homomorphism densities are nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $F$ on a finite vertex set $\alpha$ and a weighted graph $w : \operatorname{Sym}^2 V \to \mathbb R$ on a finite vertex set $V$ (unit node weights, real edge weights, loops allowed), For the $0/1$ weight of a simple graph $G$ this is the probability that a uniformly random map $V(F) \to V(G)$ is a homomorphism, and it equals $\hom(F, G) / |V(G)|^{|V(F)|}$.
nodes.title: Homomorphism density

nodes.summary: The weight `∏_{ij ∈ E(F)} w(φ i, φ j)` of a map `φ : α → V` from the vertices of a simple graph `F` to a weighted graph `w : Sym2 V → ℝ` (Lovász–Szegedy, *Limits of dense graph sequences*, §2.1, `hom_φ(F, G)` with node weights `1`).
nodes.title: Weight of a map into a weighted graph

nodes.summary: The partition average is constant on the blocks of the partition.
nodes.title: The partition average is block-constant

nodes.summary: A function `g : V → V → ℝ` is constant on the blocks `Vᵢ × Vⱼ` of a partition `P` of `V`.
nodes.title: Block-constant functions

nodes.summary: A sequence of simple graphs $G_n$ (on vertex sets $\{0, \dots, N_n - 1\}$) is convergent, or left convergent, if $t(F, G_n)$ converges as $n \to \infty$ for every simple graph $F$. The number of vertices need not tend to infinity.
nodes.title: Convergent graph sequence

nodes.summary: The normalized norm `‖G‖₂ = (|V|⁻² ∑_{x, y} w(x, y)²) ^ (1/2)` of a weighted graph with unit node weights (Borgs–Chayes–Lovász–Sós–Vesztergombi, *Convergent sequences of dense graphs I*, §2.1).
nodes.title: L² norm of a weighted graph

nodes.summary: For a partition $\mathcal P = \{V_1, \dots, V_k\}$ of the vertex set of a weighted graph $G$ (unit node weights), $G_{\mathcal P}$ is the weighted graph on the same vertices whose weight on $xy$, for $x \in V_i$ and $y \in V_j$, is the average It is the step-function approximation of $G$ with steps $\mathcal P$ that the weak regularity lemma uses.
nodes.title: Partition average of a weighted graph

nodes.summary: The energy of every partition is at most `∑_{x,y} w(x, y)²`.
nodes.title: The energy is bounded by the total mass

nodes.summary: `∑_{x,y} w_P(x, y)²`, the squared `L²` mass of the partition average.
nodes.title: Energy of a partition

nodes.summary: The common refinement of `P` with the partitions `{S, Sᶜ}` and `{T, Tᶜ}`.
nodes.title: Refinement by two sets

nodes.summary: Two vertices are related when they lie in the same class of $\mathcal P$ and on the same side of $S$ and of $T$. Its classes form the common refinement of $\mathcal P$ with $\{S, S^c\}$ and $\{T, T^c\}$.
nodes.title: Common refinement relation

nodes.summary: Refining `P` by the two sets `S, T` raises the energy by at least `|V|⁻² (∑_{x ∈ S, y ∈ T} (w - w_P)(x, y))²`.
nodes.title: Energy increment

nodes.summary: `w - w_P` is orthogonal to every function that is constant on the blocks of `P`: `∑_{x,y} (w - w_P)(x, y) g(x, y) = 0`.
nodes.title: Orthogonality of the partition average

nodes.summary: For graphons $W_n$ and $W$ with values in $[0, 1]$, The direction ⇐ is the counting lemma; the direction ⇒ is the inverse counting lemma: if $|t(F, U) - t(F, W)| \le 3^{-k^2}$ for all $F$ on $k$ nodes, then $\delta_\square(U, W) \le 22 / \sqrt{\log_2 k}$, proved by sampling.
nodes.title: Left convergence is cut-distance convergence

nodes.summary: Maps `ℝ → ℝ` preserving the Lebesgue measure restricted to `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Measure-preserving maps of the unit interval

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
